Context: Diagram `1` represents an overhead view of the movement of water and sand in a longshore current along a beach. Arrows represent direction of movement. The photograph shows groins located along the shore of Monmouth Beach, New Jersey.
Title: Longshore Currents
Content: Longshore sediment transport occurs as waves approach the shoreline at an angle. These currents carry sand parallel to the beach. The amount of sand moved along the shoreline depends on the size and velocity of the waves.

Along the shore of Monmouth Beach, New Jersey, longshore currents are present. Groins at Monmouth are structures made up of concrete or stone built out into the ocean to slow the movement of sand by these longshore currents.
